To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the presence of elemental sulfur in sediments of the Pialassa Baiona lagoon is associated to the occurrence of mercury, (ii) the highest concentrations of mercury are found in surface sediments where sulfide and S0 are also abundant, (iii) S0 is likely to be involved in the mobilization of mercury in the surface layers of the lagoon, and (iv) the role of S0 is probably related to the presence of sulfides in these sediments

Elemental sulfur (S0, a non-toxic, naturally-occurring mineral) is present in the sediments of a lagoon impacted by mercury contamination, and may play a crucial role as a sink for mercury in these environments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the occurrence of Sulfur speciation (S0, sulfates and sulfides) in sediments of the Pialassa Baiona lagoon.
the role of S0 in controlling mercury mobility in salt-marsh sediments and with the potential for the formation of mercury-sulfur complexes.
the role played by sulfur species on the mobility of mercury in salt marsh sedi- ments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the occurrence of elemental sulfur and mercury in salt marsh sedimets is not a casual event, but rather it is an example of the interaction between two natural processes, i.e. the oxidation of sulfides and the reduction of Hg2+ to Hg0.

the presence of S0 is a crucial factor in controlling Hg mobility in the sediment of the Pialassa Baiona lagoon, and that the presence of sulfides in the surface layers may also contribute to Hg mobility.
the presence of S0 and sulfides in the sediments of the Pialassa Baiona lagoon may play a role in controlling mercury mobility in these sediments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of S0 in sediments is a crucial factor for mercury mobility and bioavailability.
S0 is present in the sediments of this coastal lagoon and that it may play a role in the mercury mobility.
elemental sulfur could play a role in Hg mobility in salt marshes and that it is a key factor in Hg bioavailability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the occurrence of elemental sulfur in salt marsh sedments can be a crucial factor in determining the mobility of mercury.
elemental sulfur can play a key role in the mobility of mercury in salt marsh systems.
S0 could be a major sink for Hg in the sediments of coastal lagoons and salt marshes.
